content.title: About
content.content: Canned strawberries are whole strawberry berries that have been heat‑processed and sealed in glass or metal jars with syrup or their own juice. The berries retain their sweet flavor and much of the vitamins and minerals typical of fresh strawberries.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Strawberries are one of the few berries that contain a notable amount of vitamin C.
Canning allows strawberries to be stored for several years without losing taste.
The syrup used for canning is usually a simple sugar‑water solution, sometimes with added citric acid to preserve colour.
In the United States more than 200,000 tons of canned strawberries are produced each year.
Strawberries belong to the rose family, along with apples, pears and cherries.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and aids collagen synthesis, important for skin and blood vessels.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Flavonoids and anthocyanins in strawberries help combat free radicals, reducing the risk of chronic diseases.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Strawberries provide dietary fiber that promotes regular bowel movements.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate fluid balance and supports heart function.

items.title: Low‑calorie snack
items.content: One typical jar (about 200 g) contains roughly 70 kcal, making it a convenient light snack.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: The syrup often contains added sugar, which may be problematic for people with diabetes or those watching their weight.

items.title: Strawberry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to strawberries, ranging from skin rashes to swelling.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Certain brands may use preservatives such as potassium sorbate to extend shelf life.

items.title: Citric acid
items.content: Citric acid is sometimes added to maintain bright colour, but in large amounts it can irritate the stomach.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Canned strawberries can be eaten straight from the jar, added to yogurt, oatmeal, desserts, baked goods, or used in sauces for meat dishes. If you are monitoring sugar intake, drain the syrup before use.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened jars in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep the jar refrigerated and consume within 3–5 days. Discard if mold appears or the smell becomes off.
